D=[\begin{aligned}-1 & -2 & 4 & 6 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & -2 & 0 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -7\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $D$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =2$ is an eigenvalue of $D$
- $\lambda =-1$ is an eigenvalue of $D$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =-1$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$

activity_context.topic_title: The Characteristic Equation of a Matrix

feedback.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}2 & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2 & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14\end{aligned}].
$$

Consider the matrix $P$ given above. Which of the following statements are true?

- $\lambda =0$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- $\lambda =-14$ is an eigenvalue of $P$
- The eigenvalue $\lambda =2$ has algebraic multiplicity $2$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the matrix $\,P-\lambda I:$
﻿﻿﻿

$$
P-\lambda I=[\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}]
$$

The characteristic equation is $det(P-\lambda I)=0.$ 

Notice that we can expand the $4\times 4$ determinant across the $1$st column, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}det(P-\lambda I) & =0 \\ |\begin{aligned}2-\lambda  & -3 & -8 & 5 \\ 0 & -\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 0 & 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 & 4 \\ 3 & -2-\lambda  & 11 \\ 0 & 0 & -14-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, expanding the $3\times 3$ determinant across the $3$rd row, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}(2-\lambda )\cdot (-14-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}-\lambda  & 0 \\ 3 & -2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (2-\lambda )(-14-\lambda )(-\lambda )(-2-\lambda ) & =0 \\ (\lambda -2)(\lambda +14)\lambda (\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

So, the eigenvalues of $P$ are $\lambda =2,$ $\lambda =-2,$ $\lambda =0,$ and $\lambda =-14$  (all with algebraic multiplicity $1$).

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only."
